summary: Rapid route weight oscillation causing inference backpressure and regional p99 timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 06:12 UTC, Acme Payments reported increased p95/p99 latency and streaming cancellations for inference calls. Metrics show repeated short windows (30–90s) of elevated p99 (~3–6s) and increased open-stream cancels in us-west, while overall request rate did not increase. Impact: Customer-facing latency spikes leading to degraded checkout experiences and several timed-out requests. Environment: prod, primarily us-east control plane with egress to us-west POP for a subset of requests.

Observations: Rapid oscillation in route weight assignment detected in the routing service; traffic was being shifted back and forth between us-east and us-west POPs multiple times per minute. This induced transient queueing in downstream serving pools and led to KV-cache cold misses and tail latency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Acme Payments account with geo-fallback policy enabled (account tag: acme-payments.prod).
2) Send steady request stream at baseline QPS (~30r/s) from us-east clients with typical sequence lengths (avg 250 tokens).
3) Observe route weight change events in /metrics/routing/weight_changes and p99 latency in /metrics/serving/p99 for us-west pool.
4) Repeat while simulating small health flaps on an edge POP to trigger routing reevaluation.
logs: 2026-03-10T06:12:23Z routing.INFO weight_change account=acme-payments from_us_east=0.62 to_us_east=0.28 reason=latency_estimate
2026-03-10T06:12:26Z routing.INFO weight_change account=acme-payments from_us_east=0.28 to_us_east=0.61 reason=health_ping
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: aggressive route weight reconvergence logic reacts to noisy latency samples and small health indicator changes, causing oscillation.
Routing logs show weight adjustments every 10–30s for same account, correlated with small probe jitter on the us-west POP.
Serving pools in us-west show simultaneous KV cache churn when traffic switches, increasing per-token compute and memory pressure.
Observed that autoscaler in Dedicated pools was slow to react to the sudden burst when weight shifted (scale-up lag ~90s).
No evidence of network-level packet loss or widespread BGP events during windows — checks with peering showed stable sessions.
actions_taken: 1) Temporarily pinned Acme Payments routing policy to prefer us-east (manual override) to stabilize traffic while investigating.
2) Scoped routing logs and increased sampling to 1s for weight-change metrics for affected accounts.
3) Applied emergency tweak to routing smoothing coefficient for acme-payments to dampen weight updates (rollout 1%).
4) Notified SRE oncall to watch autoscaler for us-west serving pools and manually triggered a small scale-up to relieve queueing.
next_steps: 1) Implement a safer hysteresis for route weight changes to require sustained signal for >60s before shifting >20% of traffic.
2) Add synthetic KV cache warmup plan during weight shifts to avoid cold misses (test in staging).
3) Update autoscaler policy to consider routing-driven delta (pre-scale for anticipated short bursts).
4) Coordinate with Networking to examine health probe sensitivity and reduce noise from POP health checks.
5) Keep Acme Payments pinned until persistent fix is deployed and validated.
resolution_notes: (pending) Temporary manual pin to us-east applied. Rolling change to routing smoothing coefficient at 1% has reduced frequency of oscillation in initial sampling; need full rollout and autoscaler policy change to close.
